newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * President Emil Constantinescu has called a Supreme Defence Council meeting to adopt Romania's national security strategy focusing on security interests and local and international risk factors.
Constantinescu will present the strategy to the two houses of parliament after it has won Council approval.

* Visiting Polish Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati said considering a larger number of countries for the first wave of NATO expansion would be more beneficial for the stability of Europe and of the Alliance.
His remark followed a decision by the U.S. administration on Thursday to invite only three ex-communist countries -- Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- to join the NATO.
* Cristian Dumitrescu, vice-president of parliament's upper Senate, said a final NATO decision on eastward expansion would be reached only at the Madrid summit in July.
He said Romania's sole option would remain to join the Alliance irrespective of the Madrid decision.
* Coal miners in the Jiu valley continue protests over pay rises. They threatened to block roads unless government representatives returned to the valley to resume talks halted on Thursday night.
Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea has a meeting with leaders of the ruling coalition to discuss protests by miners.
